225: If there is an animal that is ready for [slaughter and then] eating and one wants to milk it to eat the milk, if he milks into a dish that has no food, it is forbidden. If the dish has food, it is permitted, like if the milk is used to prepare the food or if there are crumbs and the milk is absorbed into them. But one who wants to milk his whole herd is not permitted to by virtue of putting a piece of bread in the dish. Rem"a: If a non-Jew milks an animal on a holiday with the Jew supervising, there is room to permit (Rashb"a in a responsa) but the practice is to forbid, and this should not be changed. However, on a Diaspora holiday, this is permitted on the second day (Hagahot Oshri the beginning of Beitzah). Regarding whether it is permitted to tell a non-Jew to milk an animal on Shabbat, see above chapter 405 paragraph 20. And see below chapter 510 paragraph 5 regarding whether it is permitted to let milk stand [in rennet] or to make cheese on a holiday.
